# Primary Analysis: Cheatgrass and Wildlife

## Objective

MENTION RESEARCH PAPER! This document details the analysis steps used to test whther observational data is consistent with the hypothesis that cheatgrass negatively impacts large mammals, birds, butterflies. More specifically, we test whether areas with higher cheatgrass cover correlate with lower abundance and species richness of the these three taxa. Although this is an observational study that cannot confidently draw causational conclusions, this analysis will compare the statistical explanatory power of cheatgrass cover against multiple other potentially relevant environmental factors to determine which factors are most likely to be causational.

## Setup

### Libraries

```{r}
#| output: false
library(here)
library(dplyr)
```

### Data Processing

The first step is to process raw data (found in `/data/raw/`) into analysis ready formats (saved to `/data/processed/`), all following tidy data conventions.

```{r}
#| output: false
source(here::here("R", "01_vegetation_survey_processing.R"))
source(here::here("R", "02_bird_count_processing.R"))
source(here::here("R", "03_butterfly_count_processing.R"))
source(here::here("R", "04_mammal_count_processing.R"))
source(here::here("R", "05_additional_data_processing.R"))
```

This tidy data can then be converted into summary tables that formatted for the following analysis (saved to `/data/summarized/`).

```{r}
#| output: false
source(here::here("R", "06_summarize_for_analysis.R"))
```

### Import Data

The analysis will require the summarized data for the primary analysis and a small data table that contains metadata about each column. This metadata will allow easy selection of just predictor our outcome variables, for instance, allowing for automation of repeated analyses.

```{r}
#| output: false
original_data <- read.csv(here::here(
  "data", 
  "summarized", 
  "main_summary.csv"))
original_data_columns <- read.csv(here::here(
  "data", 
  "summarized", 
  "main_summary_columns.csv"))
```
